easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he will sing forever?

easy.explanation: He says, “with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness.”
easy.q: What will the psalmist make known with his mouth?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “I have made a covenant with my chosen, I have sworn unto David my servant.”
easy.q: With whom did the LORD make a covenant?

medium.explanation: The psalmist says he will make God's faithfulness known “to all generations.”
medium.q: To whom will the psalmist make known God's faithfulness?

answers: God's mercy will be established continually
Mercy will become a military fortress
medium.explanation: The expression presents God's mercy as enduring and firmly established.
medium.q: What does “Mercy shall be built up for ever” suggest?

medium.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations.”
medium.q: What did God promise to establish forever?

answers: Praise for God's mercy and confidence in His covenant with David
A request for vengeance against the nations
challenge.explanation: The verses join praise for God's faithfulness with His covenant promise to David.
challenge.q: What central idea connects verses 1–4?

challenge.explanation: These expressions stress the lasting character of God's mercy, faithfulness, and covenant.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by “for ever” and “all generations”?

answers: To proclaim God's faithfulness with his mouth
To list the names of David's enemies
To describe the construction of a temple
challenge.explanation: He declares that he will make God's faithfulness known to all generations.
challenge.q: What purpose does the psalmist declare at the beginning?

paragraphs.title: God's Greatness in Heaven and Creation

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD.”
easy.q: Who praises God's wonders?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “Thou rulest the raging of the sea.”
easy.q: What does the LORD rule?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “The north and the south thou hast created them.”
easy.q: What did God create according to the passage?

answers: No heavenly being can be compared with Him
Human rulers are greater than God
medium.explanation: The question emphasizes that none among the heavenly beings is comparable to the LORD.
medium.q: What does the question “who among the sons of the mighty can be likened unto the LORD?” teach?

answers: He is worthy of profound reverence
He is afraid of the saints
medium.explanation: The phrase describes God's holiness and greatness as deserving reverence.
medium.q: What does it mean that God is “greatly to be feared”?

answers: The changing waves of the sea
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says, “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.”
medium.q: What are the habitation of God's throne?

challenge.explanation: The passage mentions the heavens, the sea, the earth, and mountains such as Tabor and Hermon.
challenge.q: What range of creation testifies to God's greatness?

answers: His mighty rule is joined with justice, mercy, truth, and faithfulness
His power is separated from all moral qualities
challenge.explanation: The passage describes both God's strength and the justice, mercy, truth, and faithfulness surrounding His rule.
challenge.q: How are God's power and character presented together?

challenge.explanation: God's defeat of Rahab and the scattering of His enemies show His power and sovereignty.
challenge.q: What does God's scattering of His enemies with His strong arm emphasize?

paragraphs.title: David's Election and Promises of Protection

answers: All the kings of the earth
easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “I have found David my servant; with my holy oil have I anointed him.”
easy.q: Whom did God find and anoint with holy oil?

easy.explanation: God says, “mine arm also shall strengthen him.”
easy.q: What does God promise to do for David?

answers: The enemy and the son of wickedness
easy.explanation: Verse 22 says, “The enemy shall not exact upon him; nor the son of wickedness afflict him.”
easy.q: Who would not prevail against David?

answers: God appointed a strong helper or leader
medium.explanation: The phrase describes God's appointment of a mighty chosen leader.
medium.q: What does “I have laid help upon one that is mighty” mean?

answers: Anointing and the raising of David's power
medium.explanation: The oil signifies David's anointing, while the exalted horn represents his strength and honor.
medium.q: What do the holy oil and the exalted horn represent?

answers: They are adversaries whom God promises to defeat
medium.explanation: God promises, “I will beat down his foes before his face, and plague them that hate him.”
medium.q: What role do David's enemies have in these promises?

answers: David will call God his Father, God, and the rock of his salvation
David will turn away from God
David is portrayed as God's enemy
challenge.explanation: Verse 26 records David's confession: “Thou art my father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.”
challenge.q: What personal relationship between David and God is described?

answers: David's strength and honor will be raised through God's name
challenge.explanation: The horn symbolizes strength and honor, which God says will be exalted in His name.
challenge.q: What does “in my name shall his horn be exalted” mean?

answers: It moves from choosing and anointing to strengthening, protecting, and honoring him
It moves from victory to abandonment
It describes only the heavens and mountains
challenge.explanation: The verses present David as chosen, anointed, strengthened, defended, and exalted.
challenge.q: How does the passage develop the theme of David's election?

paragraphs.title: David's Status and the Covenant of His Line

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “Also I will make him my firstborn.”
easy.q: What title does God give David?

easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “My mercy will I keep for him for evermore.”
easy.q: What does God promise to keep for David?

answers: Visit their transgression with the rod
Give them an immediate new throne
easy.explanation: Verses 32–33 speak of visiting their transgression with the rod and stripes.
easy.q: What will God do if David's children forsake His law?

medium.explanation: Here “firstborn” conveys honor, priority, and elevated status among kings.
medium.q: What does “firstborn” signify in this passage?

answers: It allows discipline without removing God's lovingkindness
It removes all responsibility for sin
It guarantees that they will never sin
medium.explanation: The passage promises discipline for transgression but says God's lovingkindness will not be utterly taken away.
medium.q: How does the covenant address the sins of David's children?

medium.explanation: The throne is compared with the enduring constancy of the sun and moon.
medium.q: What do the sun and moon symbolize in the description of David's throne?

answers: Sin may be punished, yet God's covenant mercy remains
Sin has no connection to the covenant
The covenant depends on David having no descendants
challenge.explanation: The passage combines discipline for disobedience with promises that God's mercy and covenant will not fail.
challenge.q: What tension appears in verses 30–35?

answers: God's oath by His holiness and His promise not to lie
challenge.explanation: God says, “Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David.”
challenge.q: What strengthens the certainty of God's promise to David?

answers: The seed is separated from the throne
The throne is limited to one generation
challenge.explanation: The verses say David's seed will endure forever and his throne will be established forever.
challenge.q: How are David's seed and throne related?

paragraphs.title: The Crisis: Rejection of the House of David

answers: Cast him off and abhorred him
easy.explanation: Verse 38 says, “thou hast cast off and abhorred, thou hast been wroth with thine anointed.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say God has done to His anointed?

answers: His hedges were broken down and his strongholds ruined
They were moved into the mountains
easy.explanation: Verse 40 says, “Thou hast broken down all his hedges; thou hast brought his strong holds to ruin.”
easy.q: What happened to the king's defenses?

easy.explanation: Verse 42 says, “thou hast made all thine enemies to rejoice.”
easy.q: Who rejoiced over the king's condition?

answers: The covenant appears to have been rejected or set aside
The covenant was hidden from enemies
medium.explanation: The wording expresses the psalmist's distress that the covenant seems to have been nullified.
medium.q: What does “Thou hast made void the covenant” mean in the context of the lament?

answers: Broken defenses, plunder, enemies rejoicing, and shortened youth
medium.explanation: The verses describe ruined defenses, plunder, rejoicing enemies, weakened battle power, and shortened youth.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the humiliation?

answers: The king promised protection and stability is now defeated and humiliated
The covenant is fulfilled without any apparent difficulty
medium.explanation: The lament places the king's defeat against the earlier promises of protection and an enduring throne.
medium.q: How does the crisis contrast with earlier promises?

answers: How can God's anointed be rejected after receiving covenant promises?
Why do the heavens praise God?
challenge.explanation: The crisis confronts the apparent contradiction between God's promises and the king's defeat.
challenge.q: What central question arises from the crisis?

answers: Royal honor has been replaced by humiliation
The king received a new crown
challenge.explanation: The expression portrays the king as publicly covered with disgrace.
challenge.q: What does “thou hast covered him with shame” communicate?

answers: God once promised to defeat them, but now they prevail and rejoice
They first rule and then disappear
challenge.explanation: Earlier God promised to beat down David's foes, while in the crisis his enemies are given advantage and rejoice.
challenge.q: What change in the enemies' position appears in the psalm?

paragraphs.title: A Plea to Remember the Covenant

easy.explanation: He asks, “How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever? shall thy wrath burn like fire?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to end?

answers: The shortness of human life and His oath to David
Only the strength of the enemies
easy.explanation: He asks God to remember how short his time is and later recalls the oath to David.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to remember?

answers: The reproach of the mighty people
easy.explanation: Verse 50 says, “how I do bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty people.”
easy.q: What reproach does the psalmist bear in his bosom?

answers: The brevity and frailty of human life
The length of the king's reign
medium.explanation: The phrase points to the limited and fragile nature of human life.
medium.q: What does “how short my time is” emphasize?

answers: To emphasize human weakness and the need for mercy
medium.explanation: The question about death highlights human mortality and the need for God's compassion.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask whether any man can avoid death?

answers: To appeal for God to act consistently with His promise
medium.explanation: He recalls God's sworn lovingkindness as the basis for his plea.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist recall God's former lovingkindnesses to David?

answers: Human weakness creates a need for mercy, while the covenant gives the psalmist a basis for hope
The covenant concerns only the mountains
challenge.explanation: The psalmist joins the brevity of life with an appeal to God's promised mercy and oath.
challenge.q: How does the plea connect human frailty with the covenant?

answers: It shows that the disgrace of David's house is also an insult against God's anointed
It proves the enemies are faithful servants
It describes the joy of heaven
challenge.explanation: The enemies have reproached the LORD and the footsteps of His anointed.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of mentioning the enemies' reproach?

answers: From hiddenness and wrath toward a request for remembrance and mercy
From praise to a description of creation
challenge.explanation: The section begins with distress over God's hiddenness and moves toward appeals for remembrance and covenant mercy.
challenge.q: What emotional movement characterizes this section?

paragraphs.title: Conclusion of the Psalm and the Third Book

easy.explanation: The final verse begins, “Blessed be the LORD for evermore.”
easy.q: To whom is the closing blessing directed?

easy.explanation: The conclusion says, “Amen, and Amen.”
easy.q: How many times is “Amen” stated in the conclusion?

easy.explanation: The psalm ends with a blessing to the LORD forevermore.
easy.q: What appears in the closing verse despite the psalm's lament?

answers: Enduring praise and blessing directed to God
A request to end the covenant
A declaration that God has been defeated
medium.explanation: The statement is a continuing expression of praise to the LORD.
medium.q: What does “Blessed be the LORD for evermore” express?

answers: A reference to two separate kingdoms
medium.explanation: The repeated Amen strongly confirms the closing blessing.
medium.q: What does the repetition “Amen, and Amen” add?

answers: It ends the lament with an affirmation of blessing to God
It continues the description of defeat
medium.explanation: Although the psalm raises painful questions, it concludes with praise and affirmation.
medium.q: How does the conclusion relate to the psalm's crisis?

answers: He still blesses and trusts God even during crisis
He turns only to his enemies
challenge.explanation: The final blessing shows that the lament does not eliminate the psalmist's faith in God.
challenge.q: What does the ending reveal about the psalmist's faith?

answers: Lament and accusation are followed by blessing and affirmation
Creation is followed by a description of mountains only
War is followed by anointing only
challenge.explanation: The body wrestles with defeat and apparent rejection, while the ending gives a concise doxology.
challenge.q: What literary contrast stands out between the body and the conclusion?

answers: Praise of the LORD remains despite the unresolved covenant crisis
The covenant with David has completely disappeared
The enemies are the source of hope
challenge.explanation: The double Amen confirms that blessing the LORD remains appropriate even after the psalmist's complaint.
challenge.q: What is the main message of the conclusion in relation to the whole psalm?
